title: Conditional scalar-to-operator tail transfer under a per-edge norm majorant
question: Given a finite edge family and an explicit per-edge Banach-norm majorant ||K_e|| <= C*w(e), does the finite tail norm inherit the R-444 scalar shell bound C*T(R)?

finite_contract.edge_set: positive-coordinate nearest-neighbour edges in rectangular boxes

assumptions: The finite edge set, lower-endpoint radius and nonnegative scalar weight are exactly those of R-444.
For every retained edge e, a common nonnegative constant C satisfies the norm majorant ||K_e|| <= C*w(e).
The ambient scalar tail T(R) and finite-box dominance have already been audited by R-444.
The Banach or seminormed additive structure obeys the triangle inequality used by the Lean theorem.
missing_assumptions: A Q3LOCK-specific proof that the actual commutator or interaction term satisfies the per-edge majorant.
A representation-independent common core and weighted product-domain estimate.
Source-, cutoff-, volume-, shape-, phase- and history-uniform constants.
An exhaustion Cauchy theorem, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS identification and sector coercivity.
Physical-empty, continuum, Yang-Mills and mass-gap conclusions.
stop_conditions: If any per-edge majorant is not supplied, retain this as a conditional transfer and do not call it a Q3LOCK estimate.
If finite tails exceed C*T(R), fail the transfer audit and retain R-444 only.
If a hostile mutation removes the conditional boundary or adds a physical/continuum flag, reject the package.
Do not infer exhaustion convergence or a positive GNS gap from the finite transfer alone.
evidence_level: T0 / EXACT FINITE CONDITIONAL BANACH-NORM TRANSFER WITH SCALAR MAJORANT
non_claims: No Q3LOCK commutator or history-tail estimate is proved.
No actual Q3 operator term is shown to satisfy the per-edge majorant.
No weighted operator domain, common core, common alpha, exhaustion, OS/KMS/GNS or sector gap follows.
No physical-empty comparison, continuum, C6, Sector-A, Pre-A, Yang-Mills dynamics or mass-gap conclusion follows.

lean_crosscheck.role: Lean proves the finite triangle-inequality transfer in a seminormed additive group and checks the scaled R-444 tail arithmetic; Python checks the declared finite boxes and scalar dominance.

boundary: R-445 is a finite conditional norm-transfer lemma. It inherits the scalar R-444 bound only after an explicit per-edge operator majorant is assumed; it does not identify that assumption with Q3LOCK, close a common core or exhaustion, or establish any physical, continuum, Yang-Mills or mass-gap result.
